election_dates.primarySnippet: Whenever any political party holds a primary to nominate candidates for public offices to be filled in the ensuing November election, such primary shall be held on the Tuesday of the twenty-fourth week prior to the November general election in each even-numbered year or, in the case of municipalities, on the third Tuesday in July in each odd-numbered year.
election_dates.generalSnippet: "November election" means the general election held on the Tuesday next following the first Monday in November in each even-numbered year.

state_background_check.value: No — Georgia bars a person convicted and sentenced for a felony involving moral turpitude from holding any civil office (unless pardoned and restored to full citizenship rights by the State Board of Pardons and Paroles), but the U.S. Constitution's own qualifications for Congress (age, citizenship, residency) can't be added to by any state, so this doesn't reach U.S. House or Senate candidates
state_background_check.snippet: The following persons are ineligible to hold any civil office; and the existence of any of the following facts shall be a sufficient reason for vacating any office held by such person... (3) Any person finally convicted and sentenced for any felony involving moral turpitude under the laws of this or any other state when the offense is also a felony in this state, unless restored to all his rights of citizenship by a pardon from the State Board of Pardons and Paroles. Congressional qualifications are set exclusively by the U.S. Constitution, confirmed per https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/R41946.html: "the Framers intended the Constitution to be the exclusive source of qualifications for Members of Congress, and that the Framers thereby 'divested' States of any power to add qualifications."

college.snippet: Those lessons carried with him to the United States Naval Academy, where he was nominated by Senator Saxby Chambliss and trained to lead with integrity under pressure. After earning his commission, Tony became a Naval Aviator, flying the F/A-18 Super Hornet. He completed three combat deployments, leading missions in complex environments where decisions carried real consequences. He worked closely with allied forces, building trust and coordination across nations, and served with the discipline and accountability that only comes from knowing others are counting on you. After returning home, Tony continued his life of service as an attorney, fighting for families across Georgia and standing up to systems that too often fail the people they are supposed to protect. He is also a father and a coach, grounded in the same responsibilities and pressures that working families face every day. "I've led when the stakes were real. When people were counting on you to get it right. That kind of responsibility stays with you. And it's exactly what's missing in Washington." Tony is running to bring that same standard of leadership to Congress, grounded in service, tested under pressure, and focused on delivering for the people who depend on it. LEADERSHIP TESTED UNDER FIRE Three deployments. Three Air Medals. Leadership earned when it mattered most. Forged at the Naval Academy Graduated from the United States Naval Academy, Class of 2008. Built on a foundation of honor, courage, and commitment. Trained to lead, not just in theory, but in moments where leadership has real consequences. Service in Defense of this Nation Completed three combat deployments in support of Operation Enduring Freedom and Operation Inherent Resolve. Awarded three Air Medals for service in combat operations. Led missions in high-pressure environments where execution, discipline, and trust were non-negotiable. Working with Allies, Strengthening Security Served as a U.S. Navy liaison embedded with the Royal Australian Air Force, coordinating joint operations and strengthening international partnerships. Understands firsthand that America is strongest when we lead with both strength and trust. Service Didn't End with the Uniform Tony brought that same mindset home to Georgia. Not to sit on the sidelines, but to keep fighting. After leaving active duty, Tony returned home and enrolled at Georgia State University College of Law, graduating summa cum laude. As an attorney, he has represented families navigating some of the most difficult moments of their lives, fighting for due process, fairness, and accountability in systems that too often fall short. He has seen firsthand how broken policies impact real people, not in theory, but in courtrooms, in homes, and in communities across Georgia. At the same time, he built a life rooted in family and community, as a father, a coach, and a neighbor who understands exactly what working families are up against. Tony is also continuing his leadership development through the Harvard Kennedy School Public Leadership Credential, working toward a mid-career Master in Public Administration. bio_summary.value: Raised in LaGrange, Georgia, he learned early the values of discipline, accountability, and hard work as a student-athlete. Those lessons carried with him to the United States Naval Academy, where he was nominated by Senator Saxby Chambliss and trained to lead with integrity under pressure. After earning his commission, Tony became a Naval Aviator, flying the F/A-18 Super Hornet. He completed three combat deployments, leading missions in complex environments where decisions carried real consequences.

bio_summary.value: Dr. Rich McCormick has spent his life running toward the fights that matter. Raised by a single mother, he worked his way through school, became a Marine helicopter pilot, served in combat zones, earned his medical degree at Morehouse School of Medicine, and cared for Georgia families as an emergency room physician. In Congress, Rich brings the same mindset to lowering costs, securing communities, strengthening America, and making Washington work for the people it serves.
